claims.object_text: epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures (EIMFS), other early infantile developmental and epileptic encephalopathies, and focal epilepsy
claims.quote: Gain-of-function (GoF) variants in KCNT1 encoding for potassium channels are associated with different epilepsy phenotypes, including epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures (EIMFS), other early infantile developmental and epileptic encephalopathies, and focal epilepsy.

claims.object_text: fluoxetine blocks currents from both wild-type and mutant KCNT1 channels
claims.quote: Fluoxetine blocks currents from both wild-type (WT) and mutant KCNT1 channels with GoF in vitro features.
All 3 KCNT1 variants displayed GoF effects in vitro.

claims.object_text: variable reduction of seizure frequency (25-75%) with fluoxetine treatment
claims.quote: Treatment with fluoxetine caused a variable reduction of seizure frequency (25-75%).

claims.object_text: improvement in visual attention, participation, and muscle tone
claims.quote: Improvement in visual attention, participation, and muscle tone was also reported.
transient dyskinesia in 1 patient, which was probably related to an increase in fluoxetine plasma level.
